title: Platform safe save and auth env guidance checkpoint
content:
This checkpoint closes out the latest cross-site pass by focusing on discipline rather than another visible feature. After a long stretch of app work, the important question became how to save everything cleanly without flattening the differences between active repos, archive repos, and local-only runtime configuration.

What worked:

  • Active repos were saved cleanly: Auth, Dooky Detective, Jeffershizzle, and JeffersonWM all reached new save points without forcing unrelated archive history forward.
  • The archive guardrails did their job: clionidae-legacy and jeffersonwm-legacy were intentionally left untouched when their warning hooks fired, which is exactly why those protections exist.
  • Auth secret handling is clearer now: the repo/runtime distinction was documented directly inside the tracked env reference files so future work can keep real SMTP and token values in untracked .env while leaving Git history clean.

What did not work quite as well:

  • Tracked env references are still easy to misread: they look enough like live runtime files that a blind "save everything" would have created unnecessary risk.
  • Not every visual consistency pass is worth keeping: a short Perihelion banner-style comparison against Auth was tested, evaluated honestly, and then rolled back because the prior state served the app better.

The larger trajectory here is healthy: the platform keeps getting more connected, but the work is also getting more deliberate. When something works, we keep it. When something only sounds tidy on paper, we back it out and preserve the version that actually supports the site better.
